findings.text: §25's Why asserts `_bound_server_log` "stages a copy of the over-bound log as `<predecessor>.tmp` with `shutil.copyfile` before publishing it … The census reads that as a staged write that does not go through the owner", and its Deliverable instructs the node to make `_bound_server_log` publish the predecessor through `write_atomically`. That change is already present at the plan's own base revision: `reckon/serve.py:744-748` defines `stage_live` and calls `write_atomically(predecessor, stage_live, binary=True)`, and the function docstring already reads "The predecessor is published through the shared atomic writer". It is not a worktree artifact — `git log -S "write_atomically(predecessor" -- reckon/serve.py` returns one commit, `3d1ce97c6` "fix(serve): publish the rotated log's predecessor through the shared atomic writer" (2026-10-18 22:52), and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 3d1ce97c6 HEAD` succeeds against 7e4f955f6. §25's own done-when is likewise already met: `tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py` and `tests/test_request_duration_and_log_bound.py` both pass at head (54 passed, EXIT=0).
